title: What the Marketplace Accepts as Further Cost on an Appraised Claim
content:
Cost found after a loss under the Keyturn Host Protection Plan has been appraised is added to the claim that settled it rather than opened as a fresh claim.

### The further cost

The further cost accepted on a claim is the work the workshop has invoiced on the vehicle in the three months before, accepted at the marketplace's unmanaged-repair rate of 86 percent with nothing taken off for how the loss was settled, how late the cost is brought, what the host's payout account holds in reserve or how far the vehicle has been driven since, and held to the plan's supplement ceiling taken as its published share of the largest appraisal standing on the enrolment. The further cost is rounded half up to two decimal places once, on the final result, and the ceiling is applied to that rounded figure.

### The figures each plan publishes

| Plan | Supplement ceiling, percent of the largest appraisal | Supplement window, calendar days |
|---|---|---|
| Keyturn Shield 90 Host Plan | 15 | 14 |
| Keyturn Shield 85 Host Plan | 20 | 21 |
| Keyturn Shield 80 Host Plan | 25 | 30 |
| Keyturn Shield 75 Host Plan | 30 | 45 |
| Keyturn Shield 70 Host Plan | 35 | 60 |
| Keyturn Shield 60 Host Plan | 40 | 90 |

Every figure the plan publishes, its supplement ceiling and its supplement window among them, is read from the plan the enrolment is written on.

### Worked figure (hypothetical)

On an enrolment written on the Keyturn Shield 80 Host Plan whose largest appraisal standing is 8000, the ceiling is 25 percent of that, namely 2000. Where the workshop has invoiced 1500 on the vehicle in the three months before, the further cost accepted is 1290.00, being 86 percent of the work invoiced, which is inside the ceiling. Where the workshop has invoiced 4000, 86 percent of it is 3440.00 and the ceiling of 2000 governs.
